papers.title: Depth-Noise-Robust 5-DOF Robotic Grasping of Metallic Objects Using Synthetic Depth Data
papers.summary: Metallic objects with specular surfaces induce severe optical noise in depth sensors, degrading the reliability of vision-based robotic grasping. This paper proposes a five-degree-of-freedom (5-DOF) grasping framework that is robust to such optical noise, using synthetic depth data generated by a physical sensor noise model. Using the SAPIEN simulator, depth images are rendered through an active stereo sensor model combined with the Landau et al. noise model to reproduce reflection noise on metallic surfaces. papers.summary: This thesis studies an alternative method for reward-free offline reinforcement learning, investigating how well an agent can learn from a fixed dataset when reward guidance is missing, weak, or unreliable. A common way to handle this problem is behavior regularization, where the learned policy is kept close to the behavior policy that generated the dataset. This thesis studies an actor-to-behavior KL version of this idea using the Donsker–Varadhan representation of KL divergence. papers.title: Bidirectional TSCH for swarms of mobile robots in GNSS-denied environments
papers.summary: The motion control of robots within swarms depends on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), which could be unavailable in critical environments such as underground facilities, dense urban areas, or zones of conflict. papers.summary: Abstract We compared perioperative outcomes after robotic (rRC) and laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (lapRC) and assessed temporal changes in surgical approach and minimally invasive completion. Emergency undocking in robotic surgery: an international Delphi consensus study
papers.summary: Abstract Emergency undocking in robotic surgery is an uncommon but high-stakes event. Published protocols are predominantly single-institution and specialty-specific, and no multidisciplinary cross-specialty consensus exists. This study aimed to establish expert consensus on the definitions and procedural steps of safe emergency undocking. A four-round modified Delphi study was conducted with an international panel of robotic theatre team members. papers.title: Intraoral scanning accuracy and trueness for different dental restorations.
papers.summary: PURPOSE: To investigate the accuracy of digital impressions of various dental materials by comparing the scan accuracy and trueness of a handheld scanner operated by an experienced clinician, a handheld scanner operated by a robotic arm, and a tabletop scanner. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Standard-size models made from various dental materials were used. The scanners tested included a tabletop scanner, a handheld scanner operated by an experienced clinician, and a handheld scanner operated by a robotic arm. The number of triangles, average degrees, and number of vertices were recorded and compared.

papers.summary: Vehicular Edge Computing must meet strict deadlines under dynamic traffic while limiting energy use.
